newsitem.title: USA: U.S corp bond new issues seen slowing to a trickle.
newsitem.headline: U.S corp bond new issues seen slowing to a trickle.

text.p: New issuance of U.S. corporate bonds is expected to slow to a trickle on Friday, capping off a week of moderate primary market activity, syndicate officials said.
"This hasn't been a very robust week," said one high-grade syndicate official. "Friday's market should be very quiet," he said.

In the high-grade sector, Gulf Canda Resources Ltd was the only large issuer expected to tap the market on Friday. The company is expected to sell $200 million in 20-year bonds via Goldman, Sachs & Co.

In the high-yield market, AMC Entertainment Inc, one of the largest movie theater companies in the U.S., is readying a 144a offering of $200 million in 12-year senior subordinated notes via Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers Inc.
Price talk on the deal is a 275 basis point to 300 basis point spread over Treasuries, market sources said.
Also on Friday, Blue Chip Casino Inc, a company building a riverboat gaming complex in Michigan City, Indiana, plans to sell $80 million in seven-year senior secured notes via Merrill Lynch & Co.
Price talk on the deal is 13.50 percent to 13.75 percent, market sources said.
Returning to the high-grade market, one syndicate official said he expected issuance to pick up next week from this week's current levels.
"In general, this week was an aberration. People are still comfortable with the new issue market. We've had a little blip in supply, but things should pick up," he said.
High-yield activity was expected to continue at currently moderate levels, several junk syndicate sources said.
Central Tractor Farm & Country Inc, Key Plastics and Spanish Broadcasting System Inc are several companies expected to brink junk deals to market next week, market players said.
